![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14253263/assets/7c8c3764dcdd63bb7f7078ccdb729a95712f788db25fc1ba048172fc06b2b3d1.png)

Find the total area bounded by the polar curve $r=\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\theta )$ shown above.
question.worked_solution:
First, we want to find the interval for $\theta $ that corresponds to the first petal. Since the curve bounding the region crosses itself at the origin, we want to find the values of $\theta $ for which $r=0$, or 

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\theta ) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us two solutions for $3\theta \in [-\pi ,\pi ):$

$$
3\theta =-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2}\,⟹\,\theta =-\frac{\pi }{6},\frac{\pi }{6}
$$

So, the first petal is traversed for $-\frac{\pi }{6}\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{6}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14253263/assets/75e6fabf01bb0a73e17efee8d9d52d7c1e66cfd78eccd3d5c4d1f9e087335c1f.png)

Since there are $3$ petals, the total area bounded by the polar curve can be calculated as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{\text{total}} & =3\cdot {A}_{\text{petal}} \\  & =3\cdot \frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /6}^{\pi /6}{cos}^{2}⁡(3\theta )\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /6}^{\pi /6}(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡(6\theta ))\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{3}{4}{(\theta +\frac{1}{6}\operatorname{sin}⁡(6\theta ))|}_{-\pi /6}^{\pi /6} \\  & =\frac{3}{4}[(\frac{\pi }{6}+\frac{1}{6}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi ))-(-\frac{\pi }{6}+\frac{1}{6}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\pi ))) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{4}\end{aligned}
$$
